gates.title: Per-image licensing, archive capture, and public availability
gates.plan_assumption_checked: ASSET_PLAN.md:120 says the shot 'may need YouTube archival footage or AI-generated stand-in'. Checked: a YouTube-hosted clip carries no reuse permission, so YouTube leads are rights-blocked. Free stock (Pexels, Pixabay, Mixkit, Coverr) has no genuine 1990s software store footage. Archive-hosted home video exists with an uploader-asserted CC0.

gates.boundary_compliance: No account created, no terms accepted, no payment, no CAPTCHA bypass (stopped at UNT and Pond5), no watermark removal, no download.
review_questions: Legal risk: is the IA item-page CC0 dedication, applied by a third-party uploader rather than the named camera operators, acceptable for use in a public YouTube video, or must Devin obtain written permission from Dan Lynch / Ted Spero first (H02-a)?
Legal risk / privacy: the home video shows identifiable members of the public and store staff. Is that acceptable as incidental B-roll?

Taste: the best footage is launch-night event footage (balloons, crowd, a promoter in a Microsoft Office box costume), not a quiet everyday browse. Does that fit script sections 3 and 12, or does it read as 'Windows 95 launch' rather than 'buying software in the 90s'?
Taste / technical: source is SD 854x480 camcorder video. Upscale with a 4:3 pillarbox, crop to 16:9, or present in an 'archival' frame treatment?
Cost: is licensing the 1993 KXAS broadcast clip (beginning rate $90/second, not yet viewed) worth pursuing if the home-video rights cannot be confirmed?
Scope: if no archival rights path is acceptable, does Devin want a separately approved and labeled AI stand-in or staged reenactment assignment? (Not commissioned by this ticket.)
